title: Survival machine learning estimates metastasis-directed radiotherapy benefit in NPC
summary: In 1083 patients from two centers with nasopharyngeal carcinoma and exclusive distant metastasis, target trial emulation estimated a 4.2-month gain in 3-year progression-free survival restricted mean time with consolidative metastasis-directed radiotherapy after chemoimmunotherapy. A gradient boosting machine reached 3-year PFS AUROC 0.875 internally and 0.877 in a geographically external cohort, and a T-learner estimated absolute risk reductions of 21.6%, 14.7% and 5.7% by risk group. The analysis is retrospective and observational.
ai_technology: Eight survival machine learning algorithms (gradient boosting best) and T-learner treatment effect estimation
organization: Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center; State Key Laboratory of Oncology in South China

evidence.tested: Internal and geographic external validation on 1083 patients from two centers.
evidence.unknown: Retrospective observational data; treatment effects are model-based estimates; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning predicted progression-free survival and heterogeneous benefit of radiotherapy.
